title: Replying to @Allison CM My controversial take is that I tend to count...
transcript: Let's talk about the Shakespeare sequels, spin offs, adaptations, etc. that I have seen on stage. In my Shakespeare wrapped video, I mentioned doing a separate tally of these shows, but I didn't say what they were. So here you go. And we're just talking about theater shows, not films. And like I said before, the line can be very blurry and subjective about what's an adaptation versus just like a reimagined production of one of his play. But as far as straight up adaptations, maybe most famously we have West Side Story. We had other musical adaptations like Desperate Measures, the Wild West musical based on Measure for Measure. And Scotland, PA, an adaptation of Macbeth set in a fast food restaurant. This one is based on a film that's based on the play. Other adaptations of Macbeth include the play Peerless, set in a high school about a pair of twin sisters instead of a married couple. And Sleep No more, which does incorporate other source texts as well, but Macbeth is kind of the main one. Another Shakespeare adaptation set in a high school is a play whose title is Teenage D!ck, referring to teenage Richard the third. And another Richard the third adaptation that I've seen was called Seize the King, which played at Classical Theatre of Harlem. I also saw this Cirque Du Soleil show called Amaluna, directed by Diane Paulus, actually, which was based on the Tempest. We have the Pulitzer winning play Fat Ham Based on Hamlet. And of course, we have The Lion King, which is partly inspired by Hamlet. The next kind of category that I put in here are shows that use elements of Shakespeare's text but kind of do their own thing with it or around it, like Kiss Me, Kate does with Taming of the shrew. Or like this bizarre experimental riff on Hamlet from Japan called Hamlet | Toilet, which just kind of chops up and reimagines the play too much to really count it as a production of Hamlet. Or like Teatro La Plaza's Hamlet from Peru, which is more of a devised theater piece incorporating elements of Hamlet through the lens of the ensemble of actors with down syndrome. Or something like Macbeth (an undoing) which starts off feeling almost like a production of *Macbeth*, but deviates more and more as it goes along. Imagining that Lady Macbeth is a character who wakes up and realizes she's in a play I also saw the show William Shakespeare's long lost first play (Abridged). This is from Reduced Shakespeare Company, more famous for the Complete works of William Shakespeare (Abridged). But I never saw that on stage. And this one sort of tried to construct a plot that incorporated elements from all of Shakespeare's other plays. I've also seen two shows from Bedlam Theatre where they mashed up a Shakespeare play with one from a different playwright. They mashed up Julius Caesar with George Bernard Shaw's Caesar and Cleopatra. And they mashed up Romeo and Juliet with Uncle Vanya, calling it Uncle Romeo Vanya Juliet. Then we have the fanfic, if you will, the spin offs, the sequels. Most famously, Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are dead. But maybe less famous, Classical Theatre of Harlem did a sequel to Twelfth Night a couple years ago called Malvolio. And of course, Gary a sequel to Titus Andronicus & Juliet, fits into this category. But funny enough, it also fits into my next and final category, which is shows that feature Shakespeare himself as a character. We have something rotten, obviously. And of course, Shakespeare makes a brief but memorable appearance in the musical The Frogs. Again, there are many more shows out there that fit all of these categories. These are just the ones I've seen. But still, feel free to shout out your favorites in the comments.
